ai.title: DB health alerts drop stats grant gate and rank opaque buckets
ai.summary: The production database alerts in `common/src/util/db-health-alerts.ts` no longer refuse to run when the read-all-stats grant is absent: `buildActivityCoverageSql` and `buildStatementCoverageSql` report how many backends and statements the role can actually see, and `evaluateStatCoverage` turns that into an `activityBlind` / `statementsBlind` verdict instead of a single broken boolean. `buildBackendXminSql` removed the backend_type = 'client backend' predicate that discarded invisible sessions, so `oldest_xmin_age` is now paired with `visible_backends` and `opaque_backends`, and `buildStatementSnapshotSql` folds unreadable rows into a per-role `opaque:<userid>` aggregate bucket so `computeBusyBackendRank` can still rank them by delta. `evaluateBackendXmin` now returns a `BackendXminVerdict` carrying the opaque-backend count, and `computeBusyBackendRank` skips a first-seen opaque bucket rather than ranking its whole history.
ai.evidence: `common/src/util/db-health-alerts.ts` removes the boolean `pg_read_all_stats` probe (`buildPgReadAllStatsProbeSql`, `buildPgReadAllStatsMissingText`) and replaces it with `buildActivityCoverageSql`, `buildStatementCoverageSql` and `evaluateStatCoverage`; `buildBackendXminSql` drops the WHERE backend_type = 'client backend' filter so opaque backends are counted, and `buildStatementSnapshotSql` adds a `UNION ALL` bucket keyed `opaque:<userid>` for unreadable role statements.

ai.title: normalizeUrlInput prepends https for scheme-less URLs
ai.summary: Added `normalizeUrlInput` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-ads.ts`. It prepends `https://` to trimmed inputs lacking a scheme regex match (`/^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:/i`). `platformForUrl` now uses this helper before `new URL` parsing. eli5.text: When you type a website address like "x.com/my-post" into the product without including the "https://" part, it was being rejected silently, pressing Submit did nothing and no error explained why. The system now automatically adds "https://" to addresses you type without that prefix, so your website is recognized correctly. You'll notice that pasting a scheme-less URL (like "reddit.com/r/all") now works instead of failing quietly. Existing addresses that already include a scheme (like "javascript:alert(1)") are deliberately left untouched and still blocked, ensuring only the missing-prefix problem is forgiven, not malicious input disguised as a normal address.

ai.title: Picker sections group quota rows by pool, DeepSeek one-a-day ceiling
ai.summary: The model picker stopped assuming one section equals one quota pool, because DeepSeek's new one-a-day ceiling landed a second pool inside the PREMIUM section and the old Object.values(...)[0] shortcut would label the header from whichever row happened to come first. The new common/src/util/freebuff-session-pools.ts exports getFreebuffSectionQuotas, which groups a section's rows by their server-supplied pool token, picks the header from the most common pool, and returns the other rows separately in perModel keyed by model id; cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx renders those inline via formatFreebuffRowQuota, so a spent DeepSeek row now carries its own "DeepSeek: 1 of 1 used" chip instead of being mislabeled by the shared count. The wire change that makes this landable without a client release lives in common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts, where FreebuffSessionRateLimit gains optional pool and poolLabel fields that older servers omit, so getFreebuffSectionQuotas falls back to one bucket and pre-2026-08-19 servers look unchanged. common/src/util/freebuff-model-availability.ts also rewrites FREEBUFF_TIER_CHANGE_NOTICE to say the DeepSeek models now "share one session a day" rather than "V4 Flash now uses a daily session", matching the pooled reality the picker just learned to display.
ai.evidence: New file common/src/util/freebuff-session-pools.ts exports FreebuffSectionQuotas, getFreebuffSectionQuotas, and formatFreebuffRowQuota; cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx imports them and replaces the Object.values(...)[0] shortcut for sharedRateLimit with premiumSectionQuotas.header, then renders premiumSectionQuotas.perModel[model.id] inline per row; common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts adds pool?: string and poolLabel?: string to FreebuffSessionRateLimit; common/src/util/freebuff-model-availability.ts rewrites FREEBUFF_TIER_CHANGE_NOTICE.
ai.unknowns: The diff shows the client wiring and the new wire fields, but not the server-side emission of pool and poolLabel or the DeepSeek one-a-day ceiling configuration that triggers this path.

changes.what: Added the shared quota-pool grouper that splits a section's rows into a header pool and per-model remainders, with a formatFreebuffRowQuota helper for inline chips.
Replaced the Object.values(...)[0] shortcut for sharedRateLimit with getFreebuffSectionQuotas and renders each model's own-pool quota inline on its row.
Added optional pool and poolLabel fields to FreebuffSessionRateLimit so older servers omit them and getFreebuffSectionQuotas falls back to the one-pool behavior.
Rewrote FREEBUFF_TIER_CHANGE_NOTICE to describe the DeepSeek models sharing one daily session instead of V4 Flash using a daily session.
